text:
alex_w: Anyone seen the KV cache growth spike on long-chat workloads across Dedicated and Private lately? reprod on H100 on-prem and on our Dedicated cluster, but not consistent on Hosted.
maya_r: yes, saw p95 token latency creep yesterday after the 03:00 roll. memory graphs show steady KV retention — not immediate leak but growth over long contexts.
josh_t: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious whether it's paging churn vs retention.
alex_w: quick dump from the dedicated repro (trimmed):
```
kv_cache.entries: 1.1M
kv_cache.mem_total: 12.3GB -> 19.8GB (2h)
page_evictions.count: 238k
fragmentation_ratio: 1.28
last_eviction_policy: size_based_threshold=0.7
kernel_sel: aten_fast_attention (fallbacked to aten_generic at seq>1024)
```
maya_r: interesting — fragmentation seems high. on Hosted we run eviction_threshold=0.6 and aggressive prefix eviction. Dedicated default is 0.7, Private we patched to 0.75 for throughput.
priya_k: that drift in eviction_threshold across deployments smells like config drift. did the Dedicated clusters get the new jemalloc tuning? we changed retain_threshold in eks-daemonset config last month.
ops_liz: Private (on-prem) boxes are H100s with 384KB hugepages disabled due to infra constraints; NIC MTU set to 1500 (no jumbo), and we have PCIe bifurcation differences. could be affecting page migration latencies.
josh_t: also note kernel selection: on Hosted kernel picks fused_kv_kernel for quantized models, but Dedicated falls back to classic path for long sequences -> different memory layout + KV paging pattern.
infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout 2026-11-02 03:00 -> dedicated/runtime v4.9.1 applied to pool-a
maya_r: repro steps I used: run long-chat perf harness with seq=4096, bsz=1 steady-state for 2 hours, measure kv_cache.mem_total and evictions. Hosted run @ same config stays ~11GB with small evictions.
alex_w: hypothesis: combination of (1) eviction_threshold drift, (2) kernel fallback producing larger per-token KV frames, (3) smaller page alignment on on-prem -> more fragmentation.
priya_k: agree. quick mitigation options: lower eviction_threshold on Dedicated to 0.6, enable prefix-only eviction mode for long-chats, and force fused_kv_kernel selection for quantized models via runtime flag.
ops_liz: can we enable jumbo frames (MTU 9000) in Private lab to test? might reduce NIC-induced stalls during KV syncs.
josh_t: I'll run A/B with kernel_force=fused_kv_kernel on dedicated-canary and track page_evictions and frag ratio for 6 hours.
maya_r: quick data point: enabling prefix-only eviction on a repro host reduced mem growth slope by ~60% over 3h.
alex_w: sweet. let's do triage: josh run kernel-forced canary, priya push eviction_threshold change to staging orchard, ops try MTU change in lab. tag me with logs. :eyes:
priya_k: noted. will open a short PR for config sync and link here.
ops_liz: making MTU change now in lab nodes, will report infra metrics.
infra-bot: perf-alert: kv_cache.mem_total > 18GB on pool-a (2026-11-02T03:42:12Z)
josh_t: started canary run at 1965432210, logging to /var/log/kvprof/canary-kernel-forced.log
maya_r: thanks — if we see reduced fragmentation and fewer evictions that's a good signal. otherwise we might need to look at allocator differences (jemalloc vs system) across deployments.
alex_w: +1. keeping this thread as the single source for the triage. short notes only please so we can grep later.
